cover_hook: Rare monkeys just got their first-ever vaccines
caption_hook: 🐒 Brazil vaccinated black-faced lion tamarins against yellow fever for the 1st time. Fewer than 400 remain + 3 more wins 👇
question: Which made you smile most: 1, 2, 3 or 4?
share_line: Send this to the friend who loves monkeys
reel_hook: Fewer than 400 of these monkeys are left
first_comment: Bonus: the vaccine stays effective for only 3 hours once mixed, so the team had to inject all three tamarins in that window. What animal would you protect first? 🐒

stories.headline: Rare tamarins get their first-ever yellow fever shots
stories.summary: Vets in Brazil's Atlantic Forest vaccinated 3 black-faced lion tamarins, a species with fewer than 400 left and none in zoos. All 3 went back to the trees and have shown no side effects.
stories.why: One outbreak could wipe out a species this small, so a shield matters.

stories.headline: A landmine sweep turned up Korea's oldest verified gun
stories.summary: Found during a safety survey on Mount Geumseong, a 25 cm bronze hand cannon has been confirmed as the earliest authentic Korean firearm. Its inscription even names the craftsman, Suk.
stories.why: It dates to 1377 or 1437, a period with almost no surviving weapons.

stories.stat_label: had no tumour growth at 6 months
stories.headline: Vitamin B3 shows early promise against a deadly brain cancer
stories.summary: In a trial of 24 people with glioblastoma, adding high-dose niacin to standard care left 82% without tumour growth after 6 months, 28% better than past studies. Bigger tests are next.
stories.why: Survival for this cancer has barely changed in 20 years.

stories.stat_label: daily growth lines in one shell
stories.headline: A giant clam kept a 30-year climate diary in its shell
stories.summary: Counting nearly 10,900 daily lines and drilling 784 tiny samples, scientists rebuilt the Great Barrier Reef's climate month by month from 1785 to 1827. Summers then were up to 1.2°C cooler.
stories.why: Records this detailed are rare for the Southern Hemisphere's tropics.

fun_fact: Giant clams can grow 1.2 m wide, weigh over 200 kg and live for more than a century.
